subject: Media Literacy
title: How Audiences Perceive Bias
description: A quick, practical guide to How Audiences Perceive Bias.

hook.text: A study showed the same news article to liberals and conservatives. Both groups said it was biased against them.

buildup.text: The hostile media effect is the tendency to perceive neutral coverage as biased against your own views.

discovery.text: Partisans on both sides rate identical coverage as favoring the opposition, even when it's perfectly balanced.

twist.text: This means accusations of bias often reveal more about the accuser's beliefs than about the coverage.

climax.text: When everyone thinks the media is biased against them, the problem might be perception, not the reporting.

punchline.text: If both sides say it's biased, it might actually be fair.

quiz.question: What is the hostile media effect?
options: People perceiving neutral coverage as biased against their own side
